cross-006.answer: about 19% (4.8 ms of the 25 ms budget, roughly a fifth)

cross-013.answer: The Skiff port runs Tern at the Performance preset (dec-run-tern-on-skiff-at-the-performance-preset--74eqayfa83ybqpe3), which saves 1.8 ms over Quality (2.1 ms vs 3.9 ms).

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active: "Shader compile cache and build farm" (eff-shader-compile-cache-and-build-farm--6xeac11zxvwwarkn) is completed, ending with dec-turn-the-shader-compile-cache-on-for-every-farm--4rr3b12b4sasdmaj, which turned the cache on for every farm build. "Co-op rollback netcode prototype" (eff-co-op-rollback-netcode-prototype--n5ejm416kfcfap49) is abandoned via dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b, because the tide simulation cannot stay in sync or be re-run affordably under rollback.

netcode-004.answer: Rollback had to re-run the tide simulation every rolled-back frame, costing 4.8 ms on Skiff (a fifth of the 25 ms frame), and the workarounds failed: smaller windows stalled, quarter-resolution tides desynced, and leaving tides out of the snapshot broke the bit-for-bit constraint. The reason depends on the world Decision dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e (abandon decision: dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b).

ports-012.answer: They raised the floor to 576p (dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb) because caustics under saltglass shimmered badly in motion at the 540p floor even after Tern (fnd-saltglass-caustics-shimmer-at-the-540p-floor--0aa8sts89vhq1s6q: visible shimmer in 7 of 10 dune views). That decision was later superseded by a lowering to 504p.

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-008.answer: 2 times (a third failure triggers full re-review)

render-031.answer: In dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9, alpha-tested foliage cost 2.1 ms in the visibility buffer (fnd-alpha-tested-foliage-costs-2-1-ms-in-the-visibil--f3g34x2k6fs367eb), so it moved to a forward pass after the resolve, where it costs 0.8 ms. Saltglass moved there too because it needs the resolved scene to refract.

render-032.answer: Per dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e: Halcyon has no Skiff build and shipping it on only two platforms would break the one-upscaler-path Constraint, and owning Tern's code matters more for saltglass than raw quality (refraction and caustics need upscaler changes the team can make the same week, not vendor tickets, with no license to negotiate) despite Tern costing 0.7 ms more on Meridian.

render-046.answer: dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4 was reopened (2026-01-12) because the 3.1 ms cost finding that sank it was a capture error (debug flag discarded cached pages); fnd-virtual-shadow-maps-cost-1-4-ms-on-meridian-with--mwpybda1vh0ac55e shows VSM costs 1.4 ms with cached pages, less than the 1.6 ms for four cascades, and cascade seams through saltglass remained unsolved under CSM.

render-047.answer: dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1: a release-build capture showed the visibility buffer at 7.4 ms on Skiff versus 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with half-rate material resolve), so the forward+ fallback was no longer worth keeping, and maintaining two opaque paths cost about one engineer-week a month.

world-034.answer: Deferred to a post-launch patch (platform agreements missing)

world-036.answer: Per dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h (2026-04-14), fibers made crashes unreadable (41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack, blocking beta crash triage) and caused the Gull thread-local bug, while a continuation-based thread pool kept workers 93% busy vs. 95% with fibers, so the small utilisation loss was worth it.

world-051.answer: Strict IEEE float mode (dec-force-strict-ieee-float-mode-for-the-tide-simula--ecwmqt7ncjngysqw) was rejected because it only fixes the compiler, not the math library: with strict flags PC and Skiff still drifted past 1 cm at minute 11, since Skiff's sin() differs by one ulp (fnd-strict-float-mode-still-diverges-because-skiff-s--z811r28v0a1wzb13). So dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e chose 32.32 fixed point with a build-time sine table, giving bit-identical tides on every peer without any platform math library.

world-055.answer: dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew: after the cold-cache rerun (Kelp 1.1 vs Zstandard 1.3 GB/s with the 4 MB dictionary), the team kept Kelp but shrank its dictionary to 1 MB on every platform, which fixes the cache thrash on Skiff, and closed the reopened Zstandard option.
